q-56116.name: Question 2
q-56116.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the ${a}^{2}$ on one side of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}-6 & =6 \\ {a}^{2} & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the square root of both sides of the equation and solve the resulting absolute value equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{a}^{2}} & =\sqrt{12} \\ |a| & =\sqrt{12} \\ |a| & =\sqrt{4\cdot 3} \\ |a| & =\sqrt{4}\cdot \sqrt{3} \\ |a| & =2\sqrt{3} \\ a & =\pm 2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

q-111429.name: Question 3
q-111429.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the ${z}^{2}$ on one side of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{z}^{2}-\frac{25}{12} & =0 \\ 3{z}^{2} & =\frac{25}{12} \\ {z}^{2} & =\frac{25}{36}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the square root of both sides of the equation and solve the resulting absolute value equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{z}^{2}} & =\sqrt{\frac{25}{36}} \\ |z| & =\frac{\sqrt{25}}{\sqrt{36}} \\ |z| & =\frac{5}{6} \\ z & =\pm \frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
